attributes.axis_log: AXIS1 (neutral, byte-identical) moved `camera = state->cameras;` from a standalone statement preceding the loop into the for-init clause (`for (camera = state->cameras; cameraIndex < 6; ...)`) -- a genuinely different AST position, untried by the 2026-08-25 park whose recorded axes (camera-first/separate/nested, register storage, scoped opt_propagation, reversed nested assignment) all targeted the two ZERO atoms rather than the address statement. Zero effect: real 4 unchanged, object byte-identical. CONCLUSION: the address atom's placement does NOT move independently of the copy-vs-remat choice. This is mechanistically expected -- in target the `li`->`addi` dependency chain creates a one-cycle bubble that the address computation fills, whereas our two independent `li`s create no bubble and the scheduler hoists the address instead. The two components are ONE mechanism, not two.
attributes.conclusion_for_next_agent: IMPORTANT REFINEMENT to claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source: in do_camera the family appears COMPOUNDED with a 3-atom rotation, so the single-instruction rewrite that law proposes as its WebFrank candidate (`li rD,0` -> `addi rD,rS,0` under a backward-scan side condition) would NOT alone close this function -- substituting the opcode leaves `[addi r29..., li r28,0, addi r27,r28,0]`, still a rotation away from target. Closing do_camera via the postprocessor needs substitution PLUS permutation, i.e. two audit classes at once (a dataflow-equivalence obligation and a permutation obligation). Our-colouring discriminant PASSES (registers already identical), so it is not blocked on recolouring. Do not spend further source-shape probes here.
